currentContext.expansion: Midstream build-out is the largest visible programme. PNCPL (Paradip-Numaligarh Crude Pipeline) of 9 MMTPA achieved mechanical completion in November 2025 and is to be commissioned during FY27 post commissioning of NRL's expanded capacity; the DNPL (Duliajan-Numaligarh Pipeline) capacity expansion from 1.2 to 2.5 MMSCMD is under construction with completion expected by FY28 and PNGRB approval obtained in February 2026; Feeder Line construction of 3.5 MMSCMD achieved mechanical completion in October 2025 with construction underway toward mechanical completion expected by October 2026 and commissioning in FY27; and the NSPL (Numaligarh-Siliguri Pipeline) expansion takes capacity from 1.72 to 5.5 MMTPA. The existing network is 1,899 km across crude oil, natural gas and petroleum products, against a 2030 Vision of 18+ MMTPA crude oil pipeline capacity, 5.5+ MMTPA petroleum product pipeline capacity and 6 MMSCMD natural gas pipeline capacity. Downstream, the NRL capacity expansion to 9 MMT (from 3 MMTPA) is on track with 85% overall physical completion, and OIL, NRL and BPCL have signed a tripartite MoU to jointly examine a cross-country petroleum product pipeline from Siliguri to Mughalsarai via Muzaffarpur plus depot augmentation, at an estimated investment of approximately ₹3,500 crore. The Company and BPCL have also entered a collaborative framework to explore participation, via a minority equity stake, in a proposed integrated greenfield refinery and petrochemical complex at Ramayapatnam, Andhra Pradesh — 9-12 MMTPA refining integrated with a 1.5 MMTPA ethylene cracker, estimated investment approximately ₹1 lakh crore, targeted for commercial commissioning during FY 2030. In petrochemicals, capacity is to rise from 594 KTPA as at FY2025-26 toward a total of 1,058 KTPA, with new capacity timelines of FY27 and FY29 and part of the addition still in the project approval stage. In new energy, 25 CBG plants are being developed across India using MSW, agricultural residues and other organic biomass; construction is in progress at Tinsukia, Bhubaneswar, Jorhat and Agartala, with Tinsukia and Bhubaneswar targeted for commissioning by March 2027 and Jorhat and Agartala scheduled for completion by March 2028; land is secured for nine additional locations, EPC-cum-O&M tenders are floated for Cuttack and Sambalpur, and DPRs are completed for 13 further locations. DIPAM approval has been obtained for JV companies with GPS Renewables Pvt. Ltd. and Hindustan Waste Treatment Pvt. Ltd., the JVA with HWTPL having been executed. Renewable capacity stood at 188.10 MW as on 31st March 2026 against a long-term target of 5-5.5 GW by 2040; a 25 MW solar project at Namrup, Assam by JV company APGCL OIL Green Power Limited is under construction and targeted for commissioning by March 2027, and an MoU with the Government of Rajasthan covers approximately ₹4,700 crore of investment in 1,000 MW of solar and 200 MW of wind capacity by 2030. In green hydrogen, a 30 kg/day AEM electrolyser pilot plant at Jorhat, Assam is commissioned with PNGRB approval for blending up to 2% green hydrogen into natural gas; a 1 MW alkaline electrolyser plant at Nalagarh, Himachal Pradesh is under construction with HPPCL; a 10 MW plant at Duliajan, Assam is planned; and NRL is implementing a 300 kg/hr (2.4 KTPA) plant at Numaligarh through M/s Greenco ZeroC on an EPC basis while planning a tender for a 5 KTPA plant on a BOO basis under the MNRE SIGHT Scheme (Mode-2B). risks.note: Fluctuations in international crude oil and natural gas prices, geopolitical developments and changing demand-supply dynamics may adversely impact revenue realisations, profitability, cash flows and investment decisions. The exposure was visible in FY 2025-26, when average crude realisation fell to US$69.04 per barrel from US$78.09. Management mitigates through operational efficiency, production enhancement, disciplined capital allocation and diversification across upstream, downstream and emerging energy businesses.

risks.risk: Exploration success, reserve replacement and production growth
risks.note: Lower exploration success, delays in executing exploration work programmes, limited availability of ready-for-drilling locations and challenges in sustaining reserve replacement may impact future production and long-term business sustainability. This is the core structural risk for an upstream-anchored company; mitigation is accelerated seismic acquisition, increased exploratory and development drilling, advanced geological and geophysical technologies, technology partnerships and expansion into frontier basins.

risks.risk: Mature fields, ageing assets and operational disruption
risks.note: Mature fields, infrastructure constraints, operational disruptions and ageing assets may adversely affect production performance, operating efficiency and revenue generation. Mitigation is through production enhancement programmes, enhanced oil recovery initiatives, workover campaigns, infrastructure modernisation, digital oilfield technologies and continuous asset performance monitoring.

Delays in project execution, procurement of specialised equipment and services, contractor performance or cost overruns may affect production targets, project economics and capital efficiency — material given the scale of concurrent pipeline, refinery and new-energy projects. Mitigation is structured project governance, milestone-based monitoring, procurement planning, contractor performance reviews and periodic senior-management oversight.

The transition towards lower-carbon energy systems, evolving customer preferences and climate-related policies may influence long-term demand for conventional hydrocarbons and alter market dynamics. The Company is responding by investing in renewable energy, compressed biogas, green hydrogen, critical minerals and biofuels while strengthening the core E&P portfolio, and targets non-hydrocarbon businesses contributing 12-14% by 2040 — a transition whose pace is itself a risk.

Changes in government policies, fiscal regime, environmental regulations and ESG requirements may impact operations, project execution, compliance obligations and operating costs. The auditors' Emphasis of Matter draws attention to a live fiscal dispute: provision towards Service Tax / GST liability on royalty on crude oil and natural gas under the Oil Fields (Regulation & Development) Act, 1948, with ₹865.12 crore (including ₹360.42 crore interest) provided for the year ended 31st March 2026 and a cumulative ₹4,753.77 crore provided on account of disputed service tax/GST on royalty till that date.

Exploration, production and hydrocarbon transportation involve inherent operational, safety and environmental risks that could impact people, assets, communities and the environment. Mitigation is through HSE management systems, process safety programmes, emergency preparedness, asset integrity management, regulatory compliance and continuous monitoring.

risks.risk: Geopolitical exposure and financial / foreign exchange risk
risks.note: The year was marked by heightened geopolitical uncertainty, volatile commodity prices and supply-chain disruption, with escalating tensions in West Asia and consequent pressure on shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, fluctuations in foreign exchange rates, interest rates and financial market conditions may impact borrowing costs, foreign currency obligations and financial performance — relevant given the Company's overseas producing interests in Russia, Venezuela and Mozambique. Mitigation is prudent treasury management, a balanced capital structure and periodic review of funding strategy.

Increasing digitalisation across Information Technology and Operational Technology systems increases exposure to cybersecurity threats, data breaches and operational disruptions. Mitigation is strengthened cybersecurity governance, enhanced IT and OT security controls, continuous monitoring of critical systems, periodic security assessments and employee awareness programmes.

risks.risk: Human capital, stakeholder and reputational risk
risks.note: Availability of skilled talent, leadership continuity, community engagement, social unrest, legal disputes and reputational events may affect business continuity and long-term organisational performance.

thesis (one-liner): Integrated Maharatna upstream PSU pivoting from mature-onshore oil to a **production-growth + gas-monetization + offshore-exploration** story: targeting 4 MMT oil / 5 BCM gas via 100-wells/yr drilling and new evacuation pipelines, while NRL's 3→9 MMTPA refinery expansion (commissioning thru Mar'27) adds a large downstream leg. themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. The same shock ran the other way for integrated refining: RELIANCE delivered O2C EBITDA of INR 17,000cr (+17%) THROUGH the Strait-of-Hormuz closure at 96-97% throughput while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, with ethane+ROGC at ~70% of ethylene feed as distillate cracks blew out (gas oil $16 to $63, ATF $14 to $62). MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.
themes.driver: Whether the pooled/APM gas-allocation mechanism is restored (the single biggest CGD earnings variable); LNG spot price and Brent; GRM/distillate cracks; ONGC rig tenders & day-rates.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company is an integrated oil and gas business with a core focus on upstream exploration and production in Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and Rajasthan, supported by an extensive crude oil, natural gas and petroleum product pipeline network and by refining through its material subsidiary Numaligarh Refinery Limited. It sells crude oil and natural gas to domestic refiners and power/industrial consumers, produces LPG and condensate, and transports its own and third-party crude and products for tariff income. It is selectively diversifying into petrochemicals, city gas distribution, renewable energy, compressed biogas, green hydrogen, biofuels and critical minerals.

group_structure.body:
- Oil India Sweden AB — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% shareholding per Form AOC-I Part A; reporting currency Euro. Holds the joint venture Indoil Netherlands B.V.
- Numaligarh Refinery Limited — subsidiary: Material subsidiary, 69.63% shareholding per Form AOC-I Part A; refining. Holds the joint venture Assam Bio Ethanol (P) Limited.
- OIL Green Energy Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% shareholding, incorporated on 31st January 2025 for energy generation through non-conventional/renewable sources; registered office in Delhi.
- Oil India International B.V. — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% shareholding; holds a 50% stake in the JV company WorldAce Investments Limited, Cyprus, which in turn owns 100% of the voting equity in Stimul-T LLC, a Russian registered entity owning block Licence 61 in the Tomsk region. Stimul-T LLC filed for bankruptcy in the Arbitration Court of Tomsk on 10th May 2023; the court's ruling dated 8th November 2023 appointed a Temporary Manager (Bankruptcy Trustee) and initiated the supervision stage of bankruptcy, currently in progress.
- Oil India International Pte. Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% shareholding, registered in Singapore; invested in oil blocks in Russia through joint venture companies registered in Singapore. Restrictions imposed by the Central Bank of Russia (valid till 30th September 2026) prevent repatriation of declared dividends to Singapore while in force.
- Duliajan Numaligarh Pipeline Limited — JV: Extent of holding 23% per Form AOC-I Part B; significant influence from having more than 20% stake and a shareholders agreement. Referred to as DNP Limited in the related-party note.
- Brahmaputra Cracker and Polymer Limited — associate: Extent of holding 10% per Form AOC-I Part B, marked as an associate; significant influence from a 10% stake with board representation along with material transactions. Petrochemicals.

- Indradhanush Gas Grid Limited — JV: Extent of holding 20% per Form AOC-I Part B, as per the Joint Venture Agreement. Gas grid.
- Assam Petro - Chemicals Limited — JV: Extent of holding 48.80% per Form AOC-I Part B, with the right to appoint one whole time director.
- Purba Bharati Gas Private Limited — JV: Extent of holding 26% per Form AOC-I Part B, as per the Joint Venture Agreement. City gas distribution.
- North East Gas Distribution Company Limited — JV: Extent of holding 49% per Form AOC-I Part B, as per the Joint Venture Agreement. Gas distribution.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

Path: 8 → ~9.5 MMSCMD (FY28) → 13 MMSCMD (FY29); can stretch to 15 MMSCMD with 15–18 new gas/deep wells. Longer-term upstream scale-up **10→12 MMTOE by 2030**.
- **Gas price / new-well premium:** 1.5 MMSCMD allocated as **New Well Gas to NRL** (20% premium over monthly APM). Benefit accrues only *after* NRL commissioning + CGD saturation — **delay in accrual flagged**; base 8 MMSCMD stays at APM. Royalty/post-wellhead-cost reforms also recently moved in upstream's favour (more cash to E&P).
- **Capex:** OIL upstream **~₹10,000 cr/yr rollover** (last yr, this yr, next yr) for ~100 onshore wells + shallow-water. FY26 total OIL capex was **₹13,025 cr** (60% expl/dev drilling, 25% facilities/projects, 13% strategic investments). Shallow-water well ~₹800 cr each; deep-water ~₹1,200 cr each (4+4 wells, ~₹4,800–5,000 cr, Samudra-Manthan-funded). First deep-water well spud ~mid-2027.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global growth reached an annualised 3.9% in Q4 2025 and is projected to moderate to 3.1% in 2026 before improving marginally to 3.2% in 2027, assuming the Middle East conflict remains contained.
- India's growth is projected at 6.5% in FY2026-27 and steady at 6.5% in 2027, with growth accelerating to an average 7.1% during FY2027-28 and FY2028-29 assuming energy-market and supply-chain disruptions normalise by late 2026.
- OPEC and its allies are expected to adopt a calibrated approach to production during 2026-27; prevailing market expectations suggest crude oil prices are likely to remain under moderate pressure amid economic and geopolitical uncertainty.
- Global oil demand is forecast to increase by 2.5 million barrels per day between 2024 and 2030 to a plateau of approximately 105.5 million barrels per day, while world oil production capacity is forecast to rise by 5.1 million barrels per day to 114.7 million barrels per day by 2030 — an increase expected to significantly exceed demand growth.
- India is projected to be the largest single-country contributor to global oil-demand growth through 2030, with demand rising from around 4.6 million barrels per day to approximately 6.64 million barrels per day by 2030, and imports currently at nearly 89% of requirements.
- India's refining capacity of approximately 256.8 million tonnes per annum is targeted by the Government to rise to 450 million tonnes per annum by 2030, and petrochemical integration across public sector refineries is targeted to rise from approximately 7% to 25% by 2030 — supportive of the Company's NRL expansion and petrochemical foray.
- India's natural gas consumption is forecast to increase by nearly 60% by 2030, driven by city gas distribution, industrial demand and power generation, with the Government targeting a 15% share of natural gas in the energy mix by 2030 versus 6.4% in 2022.
- PNGRB has authorised a 33,592-kilometre national gas pipeline network under the 'One Nation, One Gas Grid' initiative, improving accessibility of natural gas.
- Government initiatives promoting renewable energy, biofuels, green hydrogen, Compressed Bio Gas and sustainable mobility are creating new investment avenues across the energy value chain.
- Realisation pressure was a key FY26 driver — average crude oil price realisation fell to US$69.04 per barrel from US$78.09, while gas realisation was largely stable at US$6.64 per MMBTU versus US$6.68.
- Segment revenue mix: upstream revenue of ₹20,410 crore declined 5% YoY on a 12% decline in crude realization; downstream revenue of ₹26,393 crore grew 5% YoY on higher throughput; pipeline revenue of ₹936 crore grew 63% YoY driven by a retrospective upward revision of the crude oil pumping tariff on the NBPL pipeline supplying NRL.
- NRL profitability was driven by a GRM spread of $13.43/bbl on wider crack spreads between crude and product prices, with 103% capacity utilisation on operational availability of 99.13% and a record 87.25% distillate yield.
- Adoption of advanced technologies — artificial intelligence, data analytics, digital oilfield solutions, automation and advanced drilling techniques — is expected to further enhance operational efficiency, improve reservoir management and optimise production.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Midstream build-out is the largest visible programme. PNCPL (Paradip-Numaligarh Crude Pipeline) of 9 MMTPA achieved mechanical completion in November 2025 and is to be commissioned during FY27 post commissioning of NRL's expanded capacity; the DNPL (Duliajan-Numaligarh Pipeline) capacity expansion from 1.2 to 2.5 MMSCMD is under construction with completion expected by FY28 and PNGRB approval obtained in February 2026; Feeder Line construction of 3.5 MMSCMD achieved mechanical completion in October 2025 with construction underway toward mechanical completion expected by October 2026 and commissioning in FY27; and the NSPL (Numaligarh-Siliguri Pipeline) expansion takes capacity from 1.72 to 5.5 MMTPA. The existing network is 1,899 km across crude oil, natural gas and petroleum products, against a 2030 Vision of 18+ MMTPA crude oil pipeline capacity, 5.5+ MMTPA petroleum product pipeline capacity and 6 MMSCMD natural gas pipeline capacity. Downstream, the NRL capacity expansion to 9 MMT (from 3 MMTPA) is on track with 85% overall physical completion, and OIL, NRL and BPCL have signed a tripartite MoU to jointly examine a cross-country petroleum product pipeline from Siliguri to Mughalsarai via Muzaffarpur plus depot augmentation, at an estimated investment of approximately ₹3,500 crore. The Company and BPCL have also entered a collaborative framework to explore participation, via a minority equity stake, in a proposed integrated greenfield refinery and petrochemical complex at Ramayapatnam, Andhra Pradesh — 9-12 MMTPA refining integrated with a 1.5 MMTPA ethylene cracker, estimated investment approximately ₹1 lakh crore, targeted for commercial commissioning during FY 2030. In petrochemicals, capacity is to rise from 594 KTPA as at FY2025-26 toward a total of 1,058 KTPA, with new capacity timelines of FY27 and FY29 and part of the addition still in the project approval stage. In new energy, 25 CBG plants are being developed across India using MSW, agricultural residues and other organic biomass; construction is in progress at Tinsukia, Bhubaneswar, Jorhat and Agartala, with Tinsukia and Bhubaneswar targeted for commissioning by March 2027 and Jorhat and Agartala scheduled for completion by March 2028; land is secured for nine additional locations, EPC-cum-O&M tenders are floated for Cuttack and Sambalpur, and DPRs are completed for 13 further locations. DIPAM approval has been obtained for JV companies with GPS Renewables Pvt. Ltd. and Hindustan Waste Treatment Pvt. Ltd., the JVA with HWTPL having been executed. Renewable capacity stood at 188.10 MW as on 31st March 2026 against a long-term target of 5-5.5 GW by 2040; a 25 MW solar project at Namrup, Assam by JV company APGCL OIL Green Power Limited is under construction and targeted for commissioning by March 2027, and an MoU with the Government of Rajasthan covers approximately ₹4,700 crore of investment in 1,000 MW of solar and 200 MW of wind capacity by 2030. In green hydrogen, a 30 kg/day AEM electrolyser pilot plant at Jorhat, Assam is commissioned with PNGRB approval for blending up to 2% green hydrogen into natural gas; a 1 MW alkaline electrolyser plant at Nalagarh, Himachal Pradesh is under construction with HPPCL; a 10 MW plant at Duliajan, Assam is planned; and NRL is implementing a 300 kg/hr (2.4 KTPA) plant at Numaligarh through M/s Greenco ZeroC on an EPC basis while planning a tender for a 5 KTPA plant on a BOO basis under the MNRE SIGHT Scheme (Mode-2B). Geothermal feasibility studies are underway in Arunachal Pradesh in association with CES & HS, alongside a consultancy study on repurposing abandoned oil and gas wells in the Upper Assam Basin.

management_tone.title: Management tone
management_tone.body: Confident, granular, growth-forward. CMD repeatedly emphasized "explore more, produce more," running-daily-production-records, and government alignment. moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Maharatna CPSE status with an integrated presence spanning upstream, midstream pipelines, refining, petrochemicals, city gas distribution and new energy, described by the Company as an integrated energy business model.
- Large, long-life resource base — domestic 2P reserves of 190 MMTOE maintained versus FY2024-25, a Reserve Life Index of 31 years maintained, and a Reserve Replacement Ratio of 1.02 versus 0.94 in FY2024-25.
- Extensive owned pipeline infrastructure — 1,243 km of crude oil pipelines and a 654 km product pipeline, an overall network of 1,899 km, which delivered record crude throughput of 7.453 MMT and tariff revenue.
- Balance-sheet strength and access to capital — CRISIL and CARE highest domestic ratings, Moody's Baa3 Stable and Fitch BBB- Stable, at par with India's sovereign rating.
- Technology and R&D capability — ₹173.22 crore invested in R&D (3.20% of PBT), 5 patent applications filed, DRIVE 2.0 with 10 AI/GenAI-enabled digital initiatives across the E&P value chain, and first-in-field deployments such as barefoot completion, Fishbone Completion Technology and a Real-Time Downhole Pressure-Temperature Monitoring System.
- Access to international expertise through a Technical Service Agreement with TotalEnergies for seismic interpretation, reservoir modelling and well design, and prospective joint bidding in frontier offshore basins.
- Captive downstream offtake through material subsidiary NRL, whose PAT rose 90% to ₹3,057.19 crore with distillate yield of 87.25% and capacity utilisation above 100% for the second consecutive year.
- First-mover position among Indian oil and gas PSUs in critical mineral exploration, as preferred bidder for graphite-vanadium and potash-halite blocks.
- Diversified international portfolio contributing to the reserve base — producing interests in Vankor and Taas in Russia, Carabobo in Venezuela and the Golfinho-Atum discovery in Mozambique, with FY2025-26 international production of 1.12 MMT of oil and 0.97 BCM of gas.

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- Crude price (realization $69, already 5-yr low) — direct EBITDA/PAT lever.
- Natural field decline 10–12%/yr — requires relentless 100-well/yr drilling to net +4% CAGR.
- **Gas-premium accrual delay** — new-well 20% premium stranded until NRL commissioning + CGD saturation + mainland evacuation.
- Execution: NRL 9-MMT commissioning (Mar'27) + Paradip pipeline + DFL (FY28) timelines; 7-day NRL shutdown needed to commission DNPL.
- Offshore exploration risk (first large deep-water campaign; capability gap acknowledged for deep-water field development).
- Policy dependency: Samudra Manthan mechanism un-notified (capex sponsorship terms unknown); APM/excise calibration risk.
- Operational disruption: economic blockade cost ~0.1 MMT oil + ~0.3 BCM gas in FY26.
- Mozambique geopolitical/cost-escalation; Russia-asset geopolitical overhang.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious insights
non_obvious.body:
- New-well-gas 20% premium is **definitional vs allocation** — even today's 8 MMSCMD contains "new well gas" by definition but earns APM until *allocated*; premium is a future delta, not current.
- NRL has **no excise sunset clause** even at 9 MMTPA — a durable structural margin support most miss.
- Samudra Manthan = government *capex subsidy* for deep/ultra-deep wells (₹3,200 cr stratigraphic corpus + per-well sponsorship), de-risking OIL's offshore capex without changing CPSE fiscal sharing (Cat-2/3 basins: nil revenue share, 7/15-yr deferred royalty).
- TotalEnergies is an *operator* (not service co) — TSA gives genuine technical transfer + potential co-investment, materially de-risking the offshore campaign.
- DNPL chose to stay *captive* (not common-carrier) once DFL authorized; NRL's *reseller* status (PNGRB waiver) is the mechanism to push surplus NE gas to GAIL/mainland.
- Crude write-offs in FY26 PAT — an E&P-specific one-off mgmt flagged while still holding dividend.
